predecessors.text: the six Bessarabian counties: Moldova without Transnistria

predecessors.name: Moldavian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic
predecessors.text: Transnistria, the left bank of the Dniester

ledger.x: 1940, 2 August: "The republic was formed on 2 August 1940 from parts of Bessarabia and parts of the Moldavian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic"; Bessarabia was "annexed from Romania on 28 June of that year".
1940, 2 August: the westernmost part of the Moldavian ASSR, "about 4,118 km2", joins the six Bessarabian counties.

1941: "In the summer of 1941, Romania joined Hitler's Axis in the invasion of the Soviet Union", "recovering Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina, and also occupying the territory to the east of the Dniester".
1944: "Immediately after the Soviet reoccupation, in 1944"; "By the end of World War II, the Soviet Union had reconquered all of the lost territories".
1991, 23 May: "the Moldavian parliament changed the name of the republic to the Republic of Moldova" (sovereignty declared 23 June 1990).
1991, 27 August: infobox "Declaration of Independence: 27 August 1991", recognised internationally on 26 December 1991.

certainty.note: Bessarabia's Prut and Dniester lines and the Transnistrian strip; the 1940 line with the Ukrainian SSR at Budjak and Khotin is the Ukrainian dossier's.
